M17 — Lantern Network

Lantern Network

M17
Time limit: 2 seconds Memory limit: 256 MiB Input: standard input Output: standard output Test type: single test Interactive: No

Description

A town has N lantern posts arranged along one road. Post i contributes brightness ai when it is included in a powered segment.

A segment is a contiguous interval of posts. For a segment [l,r], its total brightness is

B(l,r)=∑i=lrai.

Your task is to find the shortest segment whose total brightness is at least S.

If several shortest segments exist, choose the one with the smallest left endpoint. If no valid segment exists, report that fact.

The posts are numbered from 1 to N.

Input

The input consists of:

  • one line containing two positive integers N and S;
  • one line containing N positive integers a1, a2, ..., aN.

Output

Print two integers:

  • the length of the chosen segment;
  • its left and right endpoints.

If no segment has total brightness at least S, print:

-1 -1

The answer must satisfy:

length = right - left + 1
sum(a[left..right]) >= S

Constraints

  • 1≤N≤200000
  • 1≤S≤1018
  • 1≤ai≤109

The answer may exceed the range of a 32-bit signed integer, so use a sufficiently wide integer type for intermediate sums.

Additional observations

SituationRequired behavior
The whole array is the shortest valid segmentPrint 1 N
Multiple segments have the same lengthChoose the smallest left endpoint
No segment reaches the thresholdPrint -1 -1
A segment reaches the threshold exactlyIt is valid
The brightness values are always positive. This property is important when reasoning about how the left endpoint can move.
Optional hint

Consider maintaining a window whose total brightness is at least S. Whenever the window is valid, try removing posts from its left side while preserving validity.
